# PR #20129 CI performance investigation

Evidence was captured from head SHA `157e5333de92c7b32a31c9d2b4ac0ea077271116`, primarily from [Build pull request run 34725010710](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/actions/runs/34725010710).

## Conclusion

The delay is not runner queueing. Jobs started almost immediately (2-second median and 38-second maximum queue delay across 91 jobs). The long tail is real Gradle/test execution caused by incomplete cache reuse, and the PR's intended Develocity fix is not working in this run: every inspected Gradle job reports that `community.develocity.cloud` rejected the unauthenticated request because authentication is required, followed by `The remote build cache was disabled during the build due to errors.`

This is primarily a cache-access/configuration problem rather than a new test-runtime regression. The immediately preceding `main` build at the PR's base SHA had comparable or worse uncached runtimes. GitHub's restored Gradle User Home/local build cache still makes many PR matrix jobs fast, but its coverage is uneven, leaving a few partitions and all native jobs on the critical path.

## Slow jobs

At the last observation, 89 jobs had succeeded, one was skipped, and only `testLatestDeps2` remained running. The run was therefore gated by one actively progressing test job, not by queued work or a deadlock.

| Job | Total runtime / state | Dominant step |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `common / test2 (17, hotspot, indy true)` | 51m 36s | `Test`: 46m 53s |
| `common / test2 (21, hotspot, indy true)` | 46m 1s | `Test`: 42m 18s |
| `test-native / graalvm-native-tests (22)` | 45m 35s | `Running test`: 45m 19s |
| `test-native / graalvm-native-tests (23)` | 44m 39s | `Running test`: 44m 24s |
| `testLatestDeps1` | 39m 26s | `Test`: 33m 53s |
| `common / test0 (17, hotspot, indy false)` | 39m 26s | `Test`: 35m 43s |
| `testLatestDeps2` | still running after 55m | `Test`; logs were continuing through Hibernate Reactive, Lettuce, OkHttp, and other suites |

Fourteen completed jobs exceeded 30 minutes; four exceeded 40 minutes and three exceeded 45 minutes. Setup overhead was visible but not decisive: `Free disk space` took roughly 0.5–2.2 minutes and `Setup Gradle` roughly 0.5–0.9 minutes. Nearly all jobs began within seconds of creation.

Native tests ran because `settings.gradle.kts` is explicitly considered native-relevant by `.github/workflows/build-pull-request.yml` lines 58–64. That fan-out is expected for this PR, and the three native jobs run in parallel, so their critical-path cost is about 46 minutes rather than the sum of their runtimes.

## Cache evidence

The PR moves the Develocity `server` and `projectId` configuration outside the access-key guard, intending anonymous PR builds to read the shared cache. The server did not permit that access in this run.

Representative successful job summaries:

| Job | Gradle result | Cache result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native Java 23 | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 44m 4s` | 184 executed, 10 from cache |
| Native Java 22 | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 45m` | 184 executed, 10 from cache |
| `test2`, Java 17, indy | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 46m 51s` | 1,774 executed, 619 from cache, 32 up-to-date |
| `test2`, Java 21, indy | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 42m 16s` | 1,407 executed, 988 from cache, 32 up-to-date |
| `testLatestDeps1` | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 33m 51s` | 934 executed, 848 from cache, 32 up-to-date |
| Fast `testLatestDeps0` | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m 57s` | 759 executed, 1,010 from cache, 32 up-to-date |
| Fast `test2`, Java 25 | `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3m 14s` | 1,064 executed, 1,320 from cache, 32 up-to-date |

Each of those logs ends with the same authentication rejection and remote-cache-disabled message. The `FROM-CACHE` work in the regular and latest-dependency jobs is therefore consistent with the local Gradle cache restored by `gradle/actions/setup-gradle`, not proof that anonymous shared Develocity reads worked. The native workflow does not use `setup-gradle`, and its 184/194 executed-task result is the clearest cold-cache symptom.

The cache-hit distribution also explains the matrix imbalance: `testLatestDeps0` and `testLatestDeps3` finished around 9–10 minutes total, while partitions 1 and 2 took tens of minutes. Similarly, most common test jobs finished in 5–10 minutes, but a minority executed hundreds more tasks and became the long tail.

## Regression check

[Main build 34719062174](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/actions/runs/34719062174) ran against base SHA `723bbec482f2b30517862da16204ef900e0eed5f` shortly before this PR. Comparable jobs were already slow:

- `test2 (17, hotspot, indy true)`: 61.9 minutes on `main`, versus 51.6 minutes here.
- `testLatestDeps1`: 54.0 minutes on `main`, versus 39.4 minutes here.
- `testLatestDeps2`: 52.6 minutes on `main`; the PR job was still running after 55 minutes.
- Other `main` test jobs commonly took 30–60 minutes, and that build lasted about 87 minutes overall.

Thus the PR did not introduce a broad runtime regression. It produced substantial wins where the existing GitHub/local cache happened to hit, but did not establish the shared remote-cache reads claimed by the change. The remaining long jobs resemble normal uncached `main` runtimes.

## Recommended actions

1. **Resolve Develocity authorization first.** Confirm whether the `OpenTelemetry` project permits anonymous build-cache reads. If intended, enable read-only anonymous access server-side and rerun this exact SHA from a clean cache. Success criteria: no authentication/cache-disabled warning and materially higher `from cache` counts, especially in native and the slow partition-2 jobs.
2. **Do not expose the current write-capable access key to arbitrary PR code.** If anonymous reads are unavailable, create a genuinely read-only credential and pass it only where GitHub's trust model allows it (for example, same-repository PRs). Fork PRs will still need a non-secret fallback. The current nested reusable-workflow chain does not pass `DEVELOCITY_ACCESS_KEY` into PR jobs.
3. **Give native jobs a fallback cache.** `.github/workflows/reusable-native-tests.yml` does not run `gradle/actions/setup-gradle`, unlike common and latest-dependency jobs. Adding the same read-only Gradle User Home cache would reduce the native cold-start penalty even when Develocity is unavailable.
4. **Measure one cold and one warm rerun before changing partitioning.** Record queue time, Gradle elapsed time, executed/from-cache/up-to-date counts, and remote-cache rejection for each matrix job. A rerun of the identical SHA is necessary to separate repeatable remote hits from incidental GitHub local-cache coverage.
5. **If authenticated/cache-enabled runs still exceed the target, split or rebalance partition 2.** It is the repeated common/latest-dependency long tail. Use uncached task/test durations from a successful authenticated `main` build rather than cached PR wall time when recalculating partitions.

The deterministic `fix_ci.py 20129 --download-only` collector could not run because `gh` had no `GH_TOKEN`; the investigation therefore used GitHub Actions API job metadata and logs directly. No failing test or infrastructure wait was found in the inspected jobs.
